clue.text: Former copper taken in hand about caress and let off

parts.note: ex- is the prefix meaning former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: about here means the first piece goes around the second, wrapping it

parts.note: someone taken in hand is led, guided by the hand
a caress is a gentle pat

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman is grabbed by the hand, fondled and then released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal here, not a link; 'copper' looks like slang for a policeman but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To exculpate is to clear of blame, so an exculpated person has been let off.

clue.text: Feeling of discontent when messenger drops round

indicators.note: drops tells us to let a letter fall out of the messenger's word

parts.note: an envoy is a messenger sent on a mission
a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone grows resentful when the courier stops making rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for what someone else has, a kind of discontent.

clue.text: A Parisian about to get into twist in legislative body

indicators.note: to get into tells us the first pieces go inside the twist word

parts.note: a coil is a twist or loop
un is the French for a, as a Parisian would say it
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Frenchman tries to work his way into a contorted parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A council is an elected assembly that makes rules, a legislative or advisory body.

clue.text: Shy man's talent surprisingly discovered in northern resort

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A timid man's hidden gift is unearthed while on holiday up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges SHY MANS TALENT; the 's of man's counts as an S here. Lytham St Annes is a seaside town on the Lancashire coast in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lytham St Annes is a seaside holiday town in Lancashire, so a resort in the north of England.

clue.text: A beloved, it's said, must be informed

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word is spoken, and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: a beloved thing is a prized one, so the phrase is a prized

explanation.surface: Someone cherished is entitled to be kept in the loop.
explanation.walkthrough: A PRIZED and the answer sound the same; 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprised means told about something, made aware, which is being informed.

clue.text: All right in confinement, the first mum to bring forth

indicators.note: in confinement says one piece is shut up inside another

parts.note: Eve, in the Bible, was the first woman and so the first mother
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A new mother, safe after her lying-in, is about to give birth to her first child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confinement' is the old word for the period of childbirth, which steers the surface toward maternity.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or feeling is to call it up or bring it forth.

clue.text: New introduction for Christmas book in church

indicators.note: a new introduction means the opening letter of the Christmas word is swapped for another

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A fresh preface has been written for a festive volume read at services.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces N; the solver needs a Bible book of four letters ending OEL, and only J fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets read from in church.

clue.text: Superintend as a diocesan bishop?

definitions.meaning: to superintend is to supervise or manage
a bishop is over his see, the diocese he governs

explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; read the answer in two parts for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise work or people, which is what a superintendent does.

clue.text: Luxury-lover who is relaxed, or else taut possibly?

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker is laid-back, or else wound up tight, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges OR ELSE TAUT. The lotus-eaters of Homer's Odyssey ate a fruit that left them dreamily idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotus-eater is someone living in indolent, dreamy luxury, like those in Homer's tale.

clue.text: Boast of very small relation

parts.note: v. is short for very, and here 'small' just says to take the abbreviation
an aunt is a family relation

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a tiny family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaunt is to boast or brag about something.

clue.text: Supply second part of Bible only, being frugal

parts.note: to supply is to provide
the New Testament, abbreviated NT, is the second part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone thrifty hands out only the second half of the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means careful in planning for the future, thrifty and so frugal.

clue.text: Like some tobacco policy expected soon?

parts.note: tobacco being smoked is in the pipe
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A smoking regulation is due to arrive any day now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the pipeline is planned and on its way, so it is expected soon.

clue.text: Represented clients — artist and orchestral players

indicators.note: represented, in the sense of presented again in a new form, signals rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: An agent acted for customers and a painter and for some musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' rearranges CLIENTS and ARTIST; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarinettists play the clarinet, a woodwind instrument found in every orchestra.

clue.text: Society decayed and harboured bad emotions

parts.note: to moulder is to rot or decay

explanation.surface: A club fell into ruin and its members nursed grudges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who smouldered seethed with suppressed anger or resentment, harbouring ill feeling.

clue.text: Syrupy stuff fool fed to little animals

indicators.note: fed to says one piece goes inside another, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: moles are small burrowing animals
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dimwit is given as food to small creatures, perhaps in sticky sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left after refining sugar.

clue.text: Army officer sending out fifty in groups

indicators.note: sending out means a letter is dispatched from the officer's title

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A commander dispatches fifty soldiers in squads.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera, plural of genus, are classification groups in biology.

clue.text: Style of cleric always involved in split

indicators.note: involved in says the always word is wrapped inside the split word

parts.note: to rend is to tear or split
ever means always

explanation.surface: A priest is forever caught up in a church schism.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title or form of address used for a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Stuff transferred quietly in what could be a loud environment

indicators.note: environment here means surroundings, so the rearranged letters surround the quiet letter
what could be signals the letters a loud could be rearranged into

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Something is moved in secret amid a noisy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be' rearranges A LOUD into ULOAD, which surrounds P; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An upload is data or a file sent from one computer to a server, stuff transferred.

clue.text: Enduring pain south of US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so the pain comes after the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone suffers ongoing pain somewhere south of an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting means continuing over a long time, which is what enduring means.

clue.text: In time rodents wandering round will be cut down severely

indicators.note: in says the turned rodents go inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: wandering round means the rodents turn back, read in reverse

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: Roaming mice will soon be culled heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' tempts an anagram, but with 'round' it turns the rodents back to front; 'will be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To decimate originally meant to kill one in ten, now to reduce or destroy drastically.

clue.text: Are holy folk embracing court performer?

indicators.note: embracing means the first pieces hug the court abbreviation between them

parts.note: taken as written
St is short for saint, so SS stands for saints, holy folk

explanation.surface: A question: are pious people hugging a royal entertainer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' is taken as written; the surface reads it as a question, but it opens the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who acts on stage or screen, a performer.

clue.text: Retreat gets demeaning somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Pulling back from battle can feel humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: Disengagement is the military withdrawal of forces from contact, a retreat.

clue.text: Quickly use up some of the capacity

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
some of means only part of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Fill the space fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes ECAPA from thE CAPAcity; 'up' turns it around. 'use' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old word meaning swiftly or at speed.

clue.text: Manoeuvre to work at steadily — nothing in it

indicators.note: nothing in it means the zero goes inside the work word

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tactic of plodding on while getting nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a tactic or cunning move, a manoeuvre.

clue.text: Bring back restriction, say

parts.note: a rein is a check or restriction
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A call to restore a curb, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position, to bring back.

clue.text: Confession of trader and model

definitions.meaning: a trader might admit what he does with the words ...
a model is a perfect example or standard

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, I DEAL, a trader's admission.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect model or standard to aim at.

clue.text: Approves of old-fashioned excavations

definitions.meaning: in dated slang, to dig something is to like or approve of it

explanation.definitionFit: In old slang to dig is to appreciate; archaeological excavations are also digs.

clue.text: Irritates, having got roguish without any necessity

parts.note: to needle someone is to irritate them
sly means cunning or roguish

explanation.surface: Someone annoys others and turns mischievous for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlessly means without need, without any necessity.
